page.title: The Method: principles and reusable components
page.subtitle: how the whole instrument works, and the pieces it reuses everywhere
page.reads: This is the method-side companion to the per-node drawers. The drawers tell you what each step IS; this page tells you the concepts and components that run across all of them.

reusable_components.note: The method is built from a small set of reusable components (templates). Each is applied at many nodes, not just one. Name them once here; each node's drawer points back.

items.name: The four field-shapes
items.is: Every coded field is one of four shapes. Knowing the shape tells a coder how to fill it and a reader how to trust it.

shapes.mechanic: You must choose an allowed value; the list grows only by a locked extension (fit-or-extend).
shapes.examples: Frame's axes + their values (from the atlas reader); paradigm.stance {endorsed/invoked/subverted/denied}; lineage.borrowing_function

shapes.mechanic: Assign the item to one category from a fixed set.
A fixed battery of questions or lenses run over every item, not a value you pick.
shapes.examples: the gap loci (ask these of every gap); the 8-axis frame read (score every axis)

shapes.shape: Open field + coverage scan (scan families, name freely, and beyond)
shapes.mechanic: The name is open and emergent (anti-pre-anchoring); a checklist of kinds only reminds you to look widely, never limits the names.
shapes.examples: paradigm (scan narrative/ritual/political/literary/geographic/social, then name what you find); the move operation's TYPE (an open label per move)

items.lifecycle: A field's shape is not permanent. An OPEN field can graduate to CLOSED once breadth stabilizes its values, through a lock cycle (CLC), the same way the Frame axes started open and became a locked value-list (the atlas precedent). When it graduates, lock only the FAMILY level and keep the specifier open (the move's TYPE is open now, ~40 values on one text; after running the instrument across traditions we lock its families and keep the specifier free). VOICE, by contrast, is closed from the start because grammar bounds it (active / middle-passive / null-stative will not sprout new values across traditions). The rule: lock a field only after breadth shows the set has stopped growing; locking from one text imports that text's hypothesis (anti-pre-anchoring).
items.reuse: When a new field is added to any engine, classify it as one of these four before coding it; and record whether it is closed-from-the-start (grammar-bounded) or open-now-lockable-later (awaiting breadth).

items.name: The grain rule
items.is: A field is coded at the passage grain, the move grain, or both, wherever both carry signal.
items.mechanic: Frame/Sitz/Paradigm code at BOTH passage and move; Lineage is move-native (passage = the roll-up); Witness is text-native (transmission distance is not per-move).
items.reuse: For any new coded field, decide its grain(s) before running it.

items.name: The drawer template
items.is: Every node's drawer uses the same sections in the same order, so a reader always knows where to look.
sections: 1. Header: title, subtitle, the test pills (Cold Read, vs-Wild), the Fidelity stamp, and an honest status line
4. How it works: what you give it, what the method does, what you get back
5. The method (clean, text-agnostic): the step's grammar and the definition of every piece of it
6. The method applied: the same grammar run on the golden-path text (the worked example, with its concrete values)
7. Where the work is saved: the store, the home row, and the key (findability)
9. Made by: the scripts that produce the step and this card's data
10. What's next: the flow to the next node
11. Research view (collapsible): the receipt, how to run it, and the data source
items.reuse: Build every new drawer to this order; a reader learns it once and finds everything by position. Sections 5 and 6 hold the clean-then-applied split.

items.name: The Cold Read
items.is: The check that a card (or a coding call) is self-sufficient: give it to a fresh model with no other context and see if it acts correctly.
items.mechanic: Seven questions: orient (what/where/next) + reproduce (can you run this step) + gap-scan (what's confusing/missing) + duplication-and-tier check (MECE across black=main / grey=footnote / hidden=researcher view). Run as a small cohort; fix to convergence. Include a decoy.
items.reuse: Run on every drawer card before it is called done, and as a TIE-BREAKER to settle contested coding cells (a resolvable adjudication).

items.name: The instrument-vs-wild test
items.is: The check that our fields/definitions actually help an LLM code the text, versus a naive LLM with no scaffolding.
items.mechanic: Run the same passage two ways: instrument arm (our fields) vs wild arm (just 'what are the X?'), across several models. The primary metric is RELIABILITY: does the instrument make coding reproducible where the wild arm can't be aggregated? Breadth is the second axis (does it see everything the wild arm sees).
items.reuse: Run per coded aspect; the result sets the aspect's second pill (PASS = beats wild on reliability + breadth; PARTIAL = reliability but a gap; FAIL = wild >= instrument).

items.name: The closed/open field contract
items.is: Every field declares whether it is closed (controlled vocabulary), open (free text), or numeric, and names its vocab source.
items.mechanic: Closed vocabularies render LIVE from their store (Frame from exom_axis_vocabulary), never hardcoded, so they cannot go stale. Where a closed enum has no formal vocab table yet, it renders the distinct coded values + flags 'controlled-by-convention, formal vocab owed.'
items.reuse: Applied to every field in every aspect; pairs with the four field-shapes.

items.name: The move-grammar
items.is: The unit the whole method works on. A move is one agent doing one operation to one thing, with one result.
items.mechanic: Start a new move when the agent, operation, or result changes; when in doubt keep the move whole (under-split loses less than over-split). Moves connect (one feeds the next; one reports another's speech).
items.reuse: Every downstream step reads moves: gaps hang off them, glosses answer their questions, comparisons line them up.

items.name: The strengthening loop
items.is: How the instrument improves. The tests find where a field is weak, we strengthen it, we re-run the tests, and the pill moves.
items.mechanic: The wild test (and the Cold Read gap-scan) expose a gap. A tie-breaker (a small convergence panel of fresh models) settles the contested cells; a 3DR crit surfaces what is missing and what to sharpen. We strengthen the fields into a versioned upgrade, re-code the worked example, and re-run the instrument-vs-wild A/B. If the gap closes and reliability holds, the second pill moves from PARTIAL to PASS. The instrument demonstrably improves under adversarial testing, which is itself part of the argument.
items.reuse: Run per aspect. Paradigm is the first worked example (v1 to the 3DR-11 crit plus the tie-breaker to v2); then Sitz, Witness, Lineage.

items.name: The handle and its definition
items.is: The unit for every coded field: a handle (the term) plus a 1-2 sentence operational description that DECIDES what the thing is and lets a second coder apply it, not a gesture. The Frame axis values are the model, e.g. 'abduction: infers the best explanation, reasoning back from a surprising fact to what would, if true, make it a matter of course.'
items.mechanic: Closed-vocabulary fields draw the definition from the vocab store (Frame from exom_axis_vocabulary.definition), shared across every use. Open fields (the paradigm name, the sitz) get the description from the CODER, AT CODING TIME, per instance. The definition is operational in the Lotze sense: it says what the thing is and lets you apply it, never an aesthetic image and never a restatement of the handle.
items.reuse: Every coded field, everywhere. Produced at coding time by the coder, never back-filled by an editor or an LLM at the end. If it is not coded in the instrument, we do not use it later: the reading room and the essays are built from the coded fields, so the definition must exist as part of the code, or it does not exist.

principles.note: The load-bearing commitments the whole method runs on.

items.name: Coded at the instrument, or not used
items.principle: Everything the reading room and the essays draw on is captured AT CODING TIME, by the coder, as a handle plus an operational description. Nothing is back-filled by an editor or an LLM at the end. If a field is not coded in the instrument, it does not exist, and we do not use it later.
items.why: It is what keeps the instrument reproducible. The appearance of rigor applied after the fact (the 'magic hand') is exactly what the method forbids: a description added later is one editor's polish, not the coder's judgment, and the fidelity and instrument-vs-wild checks cannot grade a field that is not there.

items.name: Two visualization registers
items.principle: The project has two goals, so it has two kinds of visualization, chosen on purpose. ANALYTICAL: for the science (the instrument is the subject, the tests are the data); aggregate, comparative, precise. COMPREHENSION: for the reading (a single text's meaning, dwelt in, a lectio-divina and Talmud register); focused, evocative, single-instance.
items.why: The two want opposite design instincts (dense and neutral versus spare and warm). Building one with the other's instinct fails: a contemplative reading room that looks like a dashboard, or a coverage chart too pretty to read precisely. Name the register before designing the view.

items.name: One record, every output (the pinch-point)
items.principle: Decompose and Situate write into ONE assembled record per passage (the enriched move), and every downstream output reads only that record: the close read, the docent summary, the gaps, the gloss, compare, resituate, and the essays. It is the pinch-point of the bow-tie: everything on the left funnels into it, everything on the right derives from it.
items.why: Get its structure right and every output inherits the rigor; get it wrong and every output inherits the error. That is why the record's schema matters more than any single drawer or view, and why it is worth building carefully before the outputs multiply.

items.name: The record is stable, the presentation is disposable (headless)
items.principle: The enriched move lives as a defined table with fixed columns, decoupled from any surface that displays it. The reading room is one head; an essay or a model is another. Redesign the reading room's look and feel as often as you like: the surface reads from the table and renders however it wants, and the data never moves when the design does.
items.why: It is a headless (decoupled, CMS-style) content store for the reading. The same neutral-feed rule as the checkout: never marry the data to a surface. It is what lets the look and feel evolve for years without a single re-code, because insertion is stable regardless of how the room is redesigned.

items.name: Read the method clean, then the method applied
items.principle: Each drawer separates two zones and never conflates them. First the METHOD, stated clean and text-agnostic: what the step does and the definition of every piece of its grammar, with no worked-example values mixed in. Then the METHOD APPLIED: the same grammar run on the golden-path text (the worked example), where the concrete values and counts live. A definition is stated once, as a legend; the worked example shows only labeled values, never re-printing the definitions.
items.why: It keeps the reusable instrument legible on its own (you can read the grammar without the example, and reuse it on any text) and keeps the demonstration honest (the example applies the method, it does not silently redefine it). Mixing them is how invented terms and text-specific assumptions creep into what should be a portable method.

the_four_checks.note: The four checks the method runs on a card or a coded field. Rule (naming-lock, S162): card-level checks are named as short WORDS, never letter-acronyms, so none collides with CRT, which is reserved for the higher-level method below.

checks.name: Cold Read
checks.asks: Can a fresh reader act correctly from this card alone?

checks.name: Cold Start
checks.asks: Can a fresh agent find where the prior work lives (its store, its key)?

checks.name: Fidelity
checks.asks: Do the card's labels equal the real source columns, with no invented terms?

checks.name: vs-Wild
checks.asks: Does our scaffolding beat an unscaffolded LLM (primary metric: reliability)?

reserved.name: CRT = Clean Room Triangulation
reserved.is: A higher-level method (Decision 200) that serves many purposes; NOT one of the card checks. The abbreviation CRT is reserved for it. The card self-sufficiency check is Cold Read, never CRT.

the_two_pills.note: Two of the four checks render as pills on a coding card, so what we're proving is visible on the card. (Fidelity shows as a verified-stamp; Cold Start is a gate, not a pill.)
the_two_pills.cold_read_pill: Cold Read: is the card self-sufficient (a fresh reader acts correctly from it alone)? States: PASS / PARTIAL.
the_two_pills.vs_wild_pill: vs-Wild: does our scaffolding beat a naive LLM (primary metric: reliability)? States: PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL.
the_two_pills.text_exception: Text (the checkout) is not a coding step, so it carries only the Cold Read pill.

reliability_explainer.note: What the two pills certify, and where the method is solid vs still soft. Honesty is the point: an unvalidated coding scheme is just a vocabulary.
reliability_explainer.crt_certifies: That a card is self-sufficient: a fresh reader acts correctly from it alone (orient + reproduce + no confusion + MECE tiers).
reliability_explainer.instrument_pill_certifies: That our fields make coding more reproducible than a naive LLM (the reliability metric), and how broad the coverage is.
reliability_explainer.where_reliable: The SET of a passage's paradigms, the dominant, and the structured fields converge across independent coders. The move-boundary and the 8 frame axes are the most rigorously tested.
reliability_explainer.where_soft: Stance and fine-grained salience are the least reproducible; the dominant needs the manifest-salience rule (what the text foregrounds), not the deepest theological frame. Named honestly, not hidden.
reliability_explainer.adjudication: Disagreements are settled by a tie-breaker Cold Read cohort (a small cohort of fresh models), which also surfaces the definition fix that caused the split, e.g. the split that led to holding stance (own terms) / is_dominant (manifest salience) / relation_to_dominant (rival effect) strictly separate.

faq.note: Objections and answers. Consolidates the two scattered rebuttal FAQs (academic/00_thesis/METHOD_REBUTTALS_FAQ + pm/40_architecture/method_rebuttals_faq_REWORKED) + the per-node FAQs. Key ones below; full merge owed.

items.q: Isn't move-segmentation as subjective as the interpretation it claims to formalize?
items.a: The move is a container-level unit (agent-operation-result); boundaries carry a confidence flag and err toward under-splitting. Segmentation is auditable, and its reliability is measured, not assumed.

items.q: Does Situate smuggle in the conclusion (circularity)?
items.a: Situate attaches context per-field with declared inputs and gates; the bias is made visible in audit logs rather than hidden behind curatorial selection.

items.q: You built this to fit Mark 16: does it generalize?
items.a: The golden path proves the pipeline coheres on one passage; a second end-to-end run on a non-Christian text tests it out of domain. Replication failures are findings, not embarrassments.

The instrument-vs-wild test measures whether the fields make coding reproducible versus a naive LLM; reliability is graded on aggregate rates, and disagreements are adjudicated by a tie-breaker cohort.

items.q: A boundary (a silence, a move edge) is itself an interpretive claim.
items.a: Yes, and it is flagged as a claim with provenance and confidence, not presented as a neutral given.

items.q: Isn't this just close reading, or form criticism?
items.a: See positioning: the new part is reproducible multi-lens coding, the negative-space (gap/silence) focus, cross-tradition comparison, and AI-augmented inter-rater reliability.

positioning.note: What is new versus adjacent methods: the committee's first question.

vs.new: extends Sitz cross-tradition and adds the 10-category substrate, coded reproducibly rather than essayistically.
formalizes 'moves' as a coded unit with a grammar, so readings are comparable across texts, not one-off.
adds the situating layers (Frame, Paradigm, Lineage, Witness) and the negative-space (gap/silence) engine.
makes the reading reproducible (multi-lens, multi-coder, measured reliability) instead of resting on a single expert reader's authority.

open_questions.note: Named honestly so they don't hide.

items.q: Where does figuration (idioms, symbols, metaphor) live?
items.state: OPEN. Figuration is a conventional SIGN, distinct from paradigm (a SCRIPT). Candidate homes: gloss-level unpacking (now), or a dedicated figuration layer coded at the move level (later, via a CLC). Flag it to the coverage-scan, don't fold it into paradigm.
